what: A dispatched lane can stop on an interactive Bash permission prompt in a session nobody is watching, and spend its entire budget there. MEASURED 2026-09-21 on checklist row B2: the first lane reached $229.13 against a $30 ceiling and committed nothing, ending on 'git commit denied by permission rule'; the re-dispatch stalled at the same wall with its pending action readable as a COMPOUND, PIPED git command (`git fetch origin main 2>&1 | tail -5 && git merge origin/main --no-edit 2>&1 | tail -60`).
why_it_matters: It converts a four-line, fully-specified, operator-approved config edit into two dead lanes and $229, and it is silent: the lane reports `need_input` to a parent that is not watching for it, so the money is spent before anyone knows there is a question. It also means a lane's ceiling does not bound the damage, because the spend is not going into work.
